contentSections: A beautiful facade design can still go wrong on site. Panels arrive in the wrong order, brackets do not line up with the slab, scaffolding blocks the next trade, and a two week job quietly becomes six. Most of these delays are not caused by the metal. They are caused by the installation sequence. This guide walks through the real on-site sequence of a metal facade installation in India, who does what at each stage, and the mistakes that cost projects weeks.

The Short Answer

A typical metal facade installation follows eight stages: site survey, shop drawings, bracket and sub-frame setting, panel delivery and sequencing, panel fixing, joint sealing, cleaning and snagging, and handover. Skipping or rushing any one of them usually shows up later as misaligned joints, leaks or rework.

Before Anyone Reaches Site

Good installation starts in the office. Two things must be settled before the first bracket is fixed:

• Approved shop drawings. These show every panel, bracket, fixing and joint. Our guide on how metal facade engineering works explains how load and detailing turn into drawings that crews can actually build from.
  • A signed off mock-up. A full size sample section confirms colour, joint width and fixing method before thousands of panels are made.
If either is missing, the site team ends up solving design problems with a drill and a hammer.
The 8 Stages of Metal Facade Installation

1. Site Survey and Setting Out

Surveyors measure the actual building, not the drawing. Concrete slabs, columns and edges are rarely exactly where the plan says. They mark gridlines and levels that every panel will follow. Errors here multiply across the whole facade.

2. Access and Safety Setup

The crew needs a safe way to reach every part of the facade. Depending on height and building shape, this can be scaffolding, a suspended platform, a mast climber or a rope access team. Safety nets, edge protection, harnesses and a clear working zone below are essential. A facade job on a live site also needs coordination with other trades.

3. Bracket and Sub-Frame Installation

Brackets or an aluminium or steel sub-frame are fixed to the slab or wall. This is the skeleton that carries every panel. Anchors must suit the base material, whether concrete, brick or block, and be tested where specified. Brackets are set to tight tolerances because even a few millimetres of error shows as a crooked joint on the finished facade.

4. Thermal Break and Waterproofing Layers

Where the design calls for insulation, membranes or fire stops, they go in before the panels. These layers are hidden later, so they must be right the first time.

5. Panel Delivery and Sequencing

Panels should arrive labelled, packed in order and stored safely on site. Protective film should stay on until the end. Panels are lifted in the sequence they will be fixed, floor by floor or elevation by elevation. Poor sequencing means crews hunt for panels, or panels get scratched while being moved.

6. Panel Fixing and Alignment

Panels are hung or clipped onto the sub-frame, then adjusted for line, level and joint width. For systems like cassette panels, consistent gaps are a big part of the premium look. Installers check alignment frequently with string lines and levels, not only at the end of each floor.

7. Joint Sealing and Finishing

Joints are sealed or left open depending on the system design, as in ventilated rainscreen systems. Sealants must suit the metal and the weather conditions. Edges, corners and returns are inspected for neat finish.

8. Cleaning, Snagging and Handover

Protective film is removed, panels are cleaned, and the team lists every defect: scratches, dents, loose fixings, joint issues. Fixes are completed, and documents such as warranty papers and maintenance instructions are handed over. Our guide on metal facade maintenance in India tells owners what to do after this point.

Realistic Timelines

Installation time depends on facade area, height, complexity, access method, weather and how ready the building is. Instead of trusting a single number, ask your facade partner for a schedule that separates these items:

PhaseWhat to ask for
Survey and drawing approvalDates for site measurement and drawing sign-off
FabricationProduction window and delivery batches
Sub-frame installationCrew size and areas per week
Panel fixingPanels per day per crew
Sealing and snaggingTime allowed for defects
Build some buffer for monsoon. Heavy rain and strong wind stop work at height.
7 Mistakes That Cost Weeks

1. Starting without approved drawings. Changes on site are slow and expensive.
  2. Skipping the mock-up. Colour, joint and fixing problems get found only after the full order is made.
  3. Trusting drawings instead of measuring the building. Slab edges vary, so brackets do not line up.
  4. Poor panel storage. Panels left in the sun or rain, stacked badly, get scratched, bent or stained.
  5. No sequencing plan. Crews wait for the right panels, and scaffolding stays up longer.
  6. Wrong sealants or skipped drainage details. Leaks appear in the first monsoon.
  7. Rushing snagging. Small defects become arguments at handover.

What Affects Facade Installation Cost?

Installation cost depends on:

• Facade area and building height
  • Access method, such as scaffolding or suspended platforms
  • Panel size, weight and complexity
  • Number of floors and repeat details
  • Site readiness and working hours
  • Weather risk and schedule pressure

To see how these fit into the full price, read our guide to metal facade cost in India. When comparing quotes, make sure each one states what is included: sub-frame, scaffolding, sealing, cleaning and warranty.

How to Choose a Facade Installation Partner

Ask these questions before you sign:

• Do you install with your own trained crews, or subcontract?
  • Can you show similar completed projects and the installation method used?
  • Who supervises on site every day?
  • What safety systems and insurance do you carry?
  • Who fixes defects after handover, and for how long?

It also helps to understand the difference between those who design and those who build. Our guide on facade contractor vs facade designer explains who you need, and our checklist on how to choose a facade company helps you shortlist.
Frequently Asked Questions

How long does metal facade installation take?

It depends on area, height, complexity and weather. Ask for a phased schedule instead of a single date.

Can a facade be installed on an occupied building?

Yes, with careful safety planning, access control and working hours agreed with the building owner.

Does the manufacturer also install?

Some do, some work with installation partners. Responsibility is clearer when one company handles both fabrication and installation.

What causes leaks after installation?

Usually wrong sealants, blocked drainage paths, poor flashing or panel movement not allowed for in the design.

Does monsoon stop installation?

Heavy rain and strong wind stop work at height for safety. Plan buffer time if your project crosses the monsoon.
